summary.text: John Croisant is a member of the Tulsa Public Schools Board of Education, a former social studies teacher and the owner of a small insurance business. A Tulsa native, he was first elected to the board in 2020 and re-elected in 2024. He is the Democratic nominee for the open 1st Congressional District seat, running on affordability, education and protecting federal programs.

paragraphs.text: Born in Tulsa, Oklahoma; graduated from Jenks High School and earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Tulsa in 1999.
Taught social studies at Edison Prep, where he also coached, and has coached soccer; in his survey he describes himself as a former teacher and coach at Edison and the parent of an Edison student.
Owns a small insurance business, according to his survey.
Won the District 5 seat on the Tulsa Public Schools Board of Education on June 30, 2020, defeating Shane Saunders 52.4% to 47.6%, and took office July 7, 2020.
Re-elected to the board on April 2, 2024, with 77.7% of the vote against Teresa Pena; his current term ends in 2028.

In his survey, describes serving as the board's vice president, heading its finance committee, and representing Tulsa Public Schools as a director on the Oklahoma State School Board Association; he says he helped introduce a strategic plan focused on reading proficiency and college and career readiness.
Has been affiliated with the Rotary Club of Tulsa and the Tulsa Regional Chamber.
Advanced as the Democratic nominee after the June 16, 2026 primary was canceled.
